findings.claim: Suspicious sign-ins from an ASN outside the account's baseline: Cloudvault VPS (DE), 8 event(s)
Most sign-ins come from DE (8 events)
VPN appliance vpn-edge-01 (firmware 22.7R2.3) runs a product listed in CISA KEV (CVE-2026-104935, CVE-2025-22457, CVE-2025-0282, …)

actions.action: Reset credentials for s.demir@aegean.edu and revoke active sessions from Cloudvault VPS (DE).
Patch or isolate vpn-edge-01 and scan for external exploitation indicators.

risk.rationale: Verified evidence shows suspicious sign-ins from a non-baseline Cloudvault VPS (DE) (F1, LIKELY 0.75, T1078.004) and, critically, an exposure: VPN appliance vpn-edge-01 running firmware with multiple CISA KEV vulnerabilities (F3, LIKELY 0.7, T1133/T1190). F2 (most sign-ins from DE, 0.5) is weak and does not explain away F1/F3. The account-takeover chain is not confirmed (no post-compromise activity observed), so contain is not satisfied; signals are not explained away, so benign is not satisfied; F1 is not merely weak and F3 is an explicit exposure, so monitor is insufficient. Escalate to a human for KEV VPN remediation and to determine whether the VPS sign-ins constitute actual compromise.
escalate_reasons: signals of compromise without a confirmed abuse chain
